SS-TLS-001.impact: Anyone on the network path can read or change the page, including login forms and cookies, before it reaches the visitor.
SS-TLS-001.detectionNote: The final URL after redirects used http:// instead of https://.

fixes.label: Nginx: redirect HTTP to HTTPS
Apache (needs mod_rewrite)
fixes.code:
RewriteEngine On
RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [L,R=301]

fixes.label: Cloudflare
fixes.code: SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates > turn on "Always Use HTTPS"

verify: Run curl -sI http://<your-host>/ and confirm it answers with a 301 redirect whose Location starts with https://.
Open the http:// address in a browser and confirm it ends up on https://.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-001.limitations: TLS certificate validity and cipher configuration are not assessed by SecureScope.

SS-TLS-002.impact: None by itself. This is the desired behaviour; HSTS makes it stronger because browsers then skip the plain HTTP request.
SS-TLS-002.detectionNote: The scan started at an http:// address and was redirected to https://.
verify: No action needed.
SS-TLS-002.limitations: Only the scanned address was tested.

SS-HDR-HSTS-001.impact: Browsers may still try plain HTTP on a visit, which allows downgrade and protocol-stripping attacks on hostile networks.
SS-HDR-HSTS-001.detectionNote: No Strict-Transport-Security header was present in the HTTPS response.

fixes.label: Cloudflare (proxy in front of your own server)
fixes.code:
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static
Header name: Strict-Transport-Security
Value: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and check that the Strict-Transport-Security line is in the response.
If a CDN or proxy sits in front of your server, check the response that reaches the browser, not just the origin.
Run a new scan. The finding is reported as no longer detected only when a later scan no longer sees it.
SS-HDR-HSTS-001.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers. Only add includeSubDomains once every subdomain works over HTTPS.

SS-HDR-HSTS-002.impact: A short lifetime means browsers stop enforcing HTTPS sooner, which leaves a longer window for downgrade attacks.
SS-HDR-HSTS-002.detectionNote: The HSTS max-age value was below 180 days.

fixes.label: Cloudflare (proxy in front of your own server)
fixes.code:
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static
Header name: Strict-Transport-Security
Value: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and read the Strict-Transport-Security line.
Check that max-age is at least 15552000 (180 days). One year (31536000) is common.
Run a new scan to confirm.
SS-HDR-HSTS-002.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers.

SS-HDR-CSP-001.impact: Without a Content-Security-Policy, a cross-site scripting flaw anywhere on the page is easier to exploit because the browser has no limit on where scripts may load from.

fixes.label: Step 1: test without enforcing (Nginx)
fixes.code: add_header Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'" always;

fixes.label: Step 2: enforce once nothing important is reported (Nginx)
fixes.code: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'" always;

fixes.label: Apache (needs mod_headers)
fixes.code: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'"

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and look for a Content-Security-Policy line.
Open the site with the browser developer tools console open. Look for blocked-resource messages and fix the sources they name before enforcing.
Run a new scan to confirm.
SS-HDR-CSP-001.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers. SecureScope does not judge whether a policy is complete, only whether it is present and avoids unsafe script sources.

SS-HDR-CSP-002.impact: 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' lets injected inline scripts run, which removes much of the protection a CSP gives against cross-site scripting.

fixes.label: Use a per-response nonce instead
fixes.code:
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-<random per response>'
<script nonce="<same value>">…</script>

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and read the script-src (or default-src) part of the Content-Security-Policy.
Confirm it no longer contains 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' for scripts, and that the site still works.
Run a new scan to confirm.
SS-HDR-CSP-002.limitations: Static sites that need inline scripts may have to accept this trade-off or generate script hashes at build time.

SS-HDR-XCTO-001.impact: Browsers may guess a file's type from its content, which can make some uploaded or misconfigured files run as scripts.

fixes.label: Cloudflare (proxy in front of your own server)
fixes.code:
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static
Header name: X-Content-Type-Options
Value: nosniff

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and check that the X-Content-Type-Options line is in the response.
If a CDN or proxy sits in front of your server, check the response that reaches the browser, not just the origin.
Run a new scan. The finding is reported as no longer detected only when a later scan no longer sees it.
SS-HDR-XCTO-001.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers.

SS-HDR-REF-001.impact: Without a policy, the full URL of the page, including any query string, may be sent to other sites when visitors follow links.

fixes.label: Cloudflare (proxy in front of your own server)
fixes.code:
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static
Header name: Referrer-Policy
Value: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and check that the Referrer-Policy line is in the response.
If a CDN or proxy sits in front of your server, check the response that reaches the browser, not just the origin.
Run a new scan. The finding is reported as no longer detected only when a later scan no longer sees it.
SS-HDR-REF-001.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers. Browsers already apply a safe default today, so this is a hardening step.

SS-HDR-PERM-001.impact: Low. A Permissions-Policy lets you switch off browser features such as camera or location that the site does not use, limiting what injected or embedded code can ask for.

fixes.label: Apache (needs mod_headers)
fixes.code: Header always set Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"

fixes.label: Cloudflare (proxy in front of your own server)
fixes.code:
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static
Header name: Permissions-Policy
Value: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and check that the Permissions-Policy line is in the response.
If a CDN or proxy sits in front of your server, check the response that reaches the browser, not just the origin.
Run a new scan. The finding is reported as no longer detected only when a later scan no longer sees it.
SS-HDR-PERM-001.limitations: SecureScope reads the headers of one response from the address that was scanned. Other pages, error pages and API routes can send different headers.

SS-DISC-SRV-001.impact: A version number helps an attacker pick known exploits for that exact software.
SS-DISC-SRV-001.detectionNote: The Server header contained a version number.

fixes.label: Cloudflare
fixes.code: Cloudflare replaces or hides the origin Server header on proxied traffic. Check the response that reaches the browser.

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and confirm the Server header shows no version number (or is absent).
Hiding a version does not fix vulnerabilities. Keep the software up to date.
Run a new scan.
SS-DISC-SRV-001.limitations: Hiding a version does not fix vulnerabilities. Keep the software patched.

SS-DISC-SRV-002.impact: Very low. The server names its software, which is mildly useful to an attacker. Many hosting providers set this and it cannot be changed.
SS-DISC-SRV-002.detectionNote: A Server header was present without a version number.
verify: Only relevant if you control the web server or proxy.
SS-DISC-SRV-002.limitations: On managed platforms (for example a CDN) the header may not be configurable.

SS-DISC-XPB-001.impact: Reveals the framework or runtime in use, which helps an attacker target known weaknesses.

fixes.label: Nginx: remove the header from a proxied response

verify: Run curl -sI https://<your-host>/ and confirm there is no X-Powered-By line.
Run a new scan.
SS-DISC-XPB-001.limitations: Removing the header hides information; it does not fix vulnerabilities.

SS-COOKIE-SECURE-001.impact: Cookies without Secure can be sent over plain HTTP, where a network attacker can read them, including session cookies.
SS-COOKIE-SECURE-001.detectionNote: At least one Set-Cookie header had no Secure attribute. Cookie values are never read or stored.

fixes.label: Raw header
fixes.code: Set-Cookie: session=<value>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

fixes.label: Express (express-session)
fixes.code: app.use(session({ cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' } }));

fixes.label: Nginx: add attributes to cookies from an upstream app (1.19.3+)

verify: Load the page, then check the Set-Cookie headers (curl -sI https://<your-host>/) or the Application tab in the browser developer tools.
Confirm the named cookie now has the attribute that was missing.
Run a new scan.
SS-COOKIE-SECURE-001.limitations: Only cookies set on the scanned response are seen. Cookies set after login or on other pages are not tested.

SS-COOKIE-HTTPONLY-001.impact: Scripts can read cookies without HttpOnly, so a cross-site scripting flaw could steal a session cookie.
SS-COOKIE-HTTPONLY-001.detectionNote: At least one Set-Cookie header had no HttpOnly attribute.

fixes.label: Raw header
fixes.code: Set-Cookie: session=<value>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

fixes.label: Express (express-session)
fixes.code: app.use(session({ cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' } }));

fixes.label: Nginx: add attributes to cookies from an upstream app (1.19.3+)

verify: Load the page, then check the Set-Cookie headers (curl -sI https://<your-host>/) or the Application tab in the browser developer tools.
Confirm the named cookie now has the attribute that was missing.
Run a new scan.
SS-COOKIE-HTTPONLY-001.limitations: Cookies that scripts legitimately need to read (for example a theme preference) do not need HttpOnly. It matters most for session cookies.

SS-COOKIE-SAMESITE-001.impact: Without an explicit SameSite value the browser default applies, which weakens protection against cross-site request forgery in some browsers.
SS-COOKIE-SAMESITE-001.detectionNote: At least one Set-Cookie header had no SameSite attribute.

fixes.label: Raw header
fixes.code: Set-Cookie: session=<value>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

fixes.label: Express (express-session)
fixes.code: app.use(session({ cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' } }));

fixes.label: Nginx: add attributes to cookies from an upstream app (1.19.3+)

verify: Load the page, then check the Set-Cookie headers (curl -sI https://<your-host>/) or the Application tab in the browser developer tools.
Confirm the named cookie now has the attribute that was missing.
Run a new scan.
SS-COOKIE-SAMESITE-001.limitations: Only cookies set on the scanned response are seen.

SS-DIR-001.impact: A generated directory index can expose files that were never meant to be public, such as backups or configuration.
SS-DIR-001.detectionNote: The page body matched the markup that web servers generate for directory listings. This is a signature match, not a confirmed exposure. Review the page manually.
verify: Open the URL in a browser. If it still lists files, disable indexing and reload.
Check that nothing sensitive is stored in that folder at all. Hiding the listing does not protect files.
Run a new scan.
SS-DIR-001.limitations: A normal page that happens to look like a directory index can match. Compressed responses are not inspected.

references.label: CWE-548: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing

SS-SCOPE-001.impact: None. SecureScope stopped because the site redirected somewhere you have not verified.
SS-SCOPE-001.detectionNote: The response redirected to a different site.
verify: Verify and scan the destination directly if you are authorized to test it.
SS-SCOPE-001.limitations: SecureScope only follows redirects within the same site.

SS-EXPOSE-GIT-001.impact: Public git metadata can let anyone download your source history, including credentials that were ever committed.
SS-EXPOSE-GIT-001.detectionNote: The scan requested /.git/HEAD and received content in git's reference format.

fixes.label: Best fix: keep it out of the web root
fixes.code: Deploy only the built site files. Do not publish the /.git folder to the public web root.

verify: Open https://<your-host>/.git/HEAD in a browser or run curl -i on it. It should return 404 or 403, not a line starting with "ref:".
Treat any secret that was ever committed to this repository as exposed and rotate it.
Run a new scan.

references.label: CWE-538: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File

SS-EXPOSE-GIT-001.limitations: SecureScope requests one fixed path and does not download or inspect the repository.

SS-EXPOSE-ENV-001.impact: A readable .env file often holds database passwords and API keys. Anyone who can read it may be able to use them.
SS-EXPOSE-ENV-001.detectionNote: The scan requested /.env and the response looked like KEY=VALUE configuration lines. The values are never stored or shown. Review the URL yourself to confirm.

fixes.label: Best fix: keep it out of the web root
fixes.code: Deploy only the built site files. Do not publish the .env file to the public web root.

verify: Run curl -i https://<your-host>/.env. It should return 404 or 403, not configuration text.
Assume every value in the file was exposed and rotate those credentials.
Run a new scan.

references.label: CWE-538: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File

SS-EXPOSE-ENV-001.limitations: A page that happens to contain KEY=VALUE-looking lines can match. Only one fixed path is requested.

SS-DISC-SEC-001.impact: Without a security contact, researchers who find a problem may not know how to reach you, or may not report it.
SS-DISC-SEC-001.detectionNote: The scan requested /.well-known/security.txt and did not receive a valid file with a Contact field.

fixes.label: File: /.well-known/security.txt
fixes.code:
Contact: mailto:security@<your-domain>
Expires: <a date within the next 12 months, ISO 8601>
Preferred-Languages: en

verify: Open https://<your-host>/.well-known/security.txt. It should return the file, not an error or your home page.
Check that it has a Contact line and an Expires date in the future.
Run a new scan.
SS-DISC-SEC-001.limitations: This is a good-practice item. It is not a vulnerability and does not reduce the score.

SS-TLS-CERT-001.impact: An expired certificate makes browsers show a full-page warning and breaks API clients.
SS-TLS-CERT-001.detectionNote: The certificate on the verified connection expires soon.

fixes.label: Renew with an ACME client (certbot example)
fixes.code:
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
sudo certbot renew

fixes.label: Managed hosting or Cloudflare
fixes.code: Turn on automatic certificate renewal in your host's TLS settings.

verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-001.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-TLS-CERT-002.impact: Browsers refuse the connection or warn visitors.
SS-TLS-CERT-002.detectionNote: The certificate's end date has passed.

fixes.label: Renew with an ACME client (certbot example)
fixes.code:
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
sudo certbot renew

fixes.label: Managed hosting or Cloudflare
fixes.code: Turn on automatic certificate renewal in your host's TLS settings.

verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-002.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-TLS-CERT-003.impact: Browsers warn visitors because the certificate was issued for a different name.
SS-TLS-CERT-003.detectionNote: The certificate does not list the scanned host name.
verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-003.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-TLS-CERT-004.impact: Browsers warn visitors because the issuer is not trusted.
SS-TLS-CERT-004.detectionNote: Verification against the standard trust store failed.

fixes.label: Use a public certificate authority and send the full chain

verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-004.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-TLS-CERT-005.impact: Clients may reject the certificate until its start date.
SS-TLS-CERT-005.detectionNote: The certificate's start date is in the future.

fixes.label: Check the server clock and the certificate dates

verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-005.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-TLS-CERT-006.detectionNote: Standard verification failed for a reason other than expiry, name or issuer.
verify: Run openssl s_client -connect <your-host>:443 -servername <your-host> </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates and check the dates.
Confirm every server and CDN edge presents the new certificate.
Run a new scan.
SS-TLS-CERT-006.limitations: SecureScope makes one TLS connection to the scanned host. Other hosts, ports and certificates are not checked.

SS-MIX-001.impact: Code, frames or form targets loaded over plain HTTP can be replaced by anyone on the network, so an attacker can run their own script on an otherwise secure page or read what a visitor types.
SS-MIX-001.detectionNote: The page's HTML contained a script, stylesheet, frame, embed or form address that begins with http://, on a page served over HTTPS.

fixes.label: Find and change the address in the template
Ask browsers to upgrade leftovers while you fix them (CSP)

verify: Open the page and view its source. Search for "http://" and confirm no script, link, iframe, embed or form uses it.
Open the browser's developer tools and check the Console for mixed content messages.
Run a new scan.
SS-MIX-001.limitations: Only the first part of the home page is read, and only resources written in the HTML. Addresses added later by scripts are not seen.

SS-MIX-002.impact: Images and media loaded over HTTP can be swapped or observed on the network, and the browser may show the page as not fully secure.
SS-MIX-002.detectionNote: The page's HTML contained an image, audio, video or similar address that begins with http://, on a page served over HTTPS.
verify: View the page source and search for "http://".
Check the browser's developer tools for mixed content warnings.
Run a new scan.
SS-MIX-002.limitations: Only the first part of the home page is read, and only addresses written in the HTML.

SS-SRI-001.impact: If a third-party host is compromised, the code it serves runs on your page with full access to it. An integrity hash makes the browser refuse a file that has changed.
SS-SRI-001.detectionNote: The page's HTML loads a script or stylesheet from another host without an integrity attribute.

fixes.label: Add the hash and crossorigin to a fixed file
Create the hash
fixes.code: curl -s https://cdn.example.net/lib-1.2.3.min.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A

verify: View the page source and confirm each third-party script and stylesheet has an integrity attribute, or is one you cannot pin.
Load the page and check the Console for integrity errors.
Run a new scan.
SS-SRI-001.limitations: Files that change without notice, such as many analytics and tag-manager scripts, cannot be pinned. Hosting a copy yourself is the alternative. Only addresses in the HTML are seen.

SS-CORS-001.impact: A policy that allows any origin together with credentials shows no list of trusted sites exists. If a server fixes the error by echoing back any origin, other websites can read a signed-in visitor's data.
SS-CORS-001.detectionNote: The response carried Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

fixes.label: Allow named origins only
fixes.code:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin

verify: Request the page and read the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. It should be one named origin, not *.
Run a new scan.
SS-CORS-001.limitations: The scan sends no Origin header, so it cannot test whether the server echoes back arbitrary origins. It reports only what the page's own response says.

SS-CORS-002.impact: Sandboxed frames, local files and some redirects send the origin "null". Allowing it lets pages anyone can build read responses from this site.

fixes.label: Remove null from the allow list

verify: Request the page and confirm the header is not null.
Run a new scan.
SS-CORS-002.limitations: Only the single response the scan fetched is read.

SS-DISC-ROBOTS-001.impact: robots.txt is public. Listing an admin, backup or configuration path tells every visitor where to look, and hiding a path this way does not protect it.
SS-DISC-ROBOTS-001.detectionNote: A line in /robots.txt contains a word such as admin, backup, staging or config. This is a name match, not proof that the path is sensitive.

fixes.label: Protect the path, then drop it from robots.txt
fixes.code:
# Put the area behind a login or an IP allow-list on the server.
# Keep robots.txt to what search engines should skip, for example:
User-agent: *
Disallow: /search

verify: Open https://<your-host>/robots.txt and read the listed paths.
Open each path in a private window. It should ask for a login or return an error.
Run a new scan.
SS-DISC-ROBOTS-001.limitations: This is a good-practice item. A harmless path with an alarming name will match, so read the list before acting.

SS-DISC-SITEMAP-001.impact: A sitemap is meant to list public pages. Admin, backup or configuration addresses in it are advertised to search engines and to anyone who opens the file.
SS-DISC-SITEMAP-001.detectionNote: An address in /sitemap.xml contains a word such as admin, backup, staging or config. This is a name match, not proof that the page is sensitive.

fixes.label: Remove the address from the sitemap
fixes.code: <!-- Delete the <url> entry that points at the admin or backup address, and protect that address with a login. -->

verify: Open https://<your-host>/sitemap.xml and look for the listed addresses.
Open each in a private window. It should ask for a login or return an error.
Run a new scan.
SS-DISC-SITEMAP-001.limitations: This is a good-practice item. Only /sitemap.xml itself is read; sitemap index files that point to others are not followed.

SS-DNS-SPF-001.impact: Anyone can send email that claims to come from your domain, and your real mail is more likely to be marked as spam.
SS-DNS-SPF-001.detectionNote: The domain's TXT records contain no record that starts with v=spf1.

fixes.label: Domain that sends email through a provider
fixes.code:
Type: TXT
Name: @
Value: v=spf1 include:_spf.<your-mail-provider> ~all

verify: Run: dig +short TXT <your-domain> and look for one line starting with v=spf1.
Send a test mail to a mailbox you control and check that SPF passes in the message headers.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-SPF-001.limitations: Only the domain you verified is read. Mail sent from subdomains has its own records. Whether the domain sends email at all is unknown to the scan.

SS-DNS-SPF-002.impact: A record ending in +all or ?all lets every server send mail as your domain, or says nothing about it, so it gives no protection.
SS-DNS-SPF-002.detectionNote: The SPF record ends in +all, ?all or a bare all.

fixes.label: End the record with a soft fail or reject

verify: Run: dig +short TXT <your-domain> and confirm the SPF record ends in ~all or -all.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-SPF-002.limitations: List every real sender before using -all, or legitimate mail may be rejected.

SS-DNS-SPF-003.impact: With more than one SPF record, receiving servers treat SPF as broken and ignore it, so it protects nothing.
SS-DNS-SPF-003.detectionNote: The domain has more than one TXT record that starts with v=spf1.
verify: Run: dig +short TXT <your-domain> and confirm exactly one line starts with v=spf1.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-SPF-003.limitations: Merging records can exceed the limit of ten DNS lookups. Check the result with an SPF validator.

SS-DNS-DMARC-001.impact: Receiving servers have no instruction for mail that fails SPF and DKIM, so spoofed mail from your domain is delivered as normal, and you get no reports about misuse.
SS-DNS-DMARC-001.detectionNote: No TXT record starting with v=DMARC1 exists at _dmarc.<domain>.

fixes.label: Start by monitoring
fixes.code:
Type: TXT
Name: _dmarc
Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@<your-domain>

verify: Run: dig +short TXT _dmarc.<your-domain> and confirm the record is returned.
Read the reports for a few weeks, then move to p=quarantine and p=reject.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-DMARC-001.limitations: Only the verified domain itself is read. DMARC for subdomains follows the parent's policy unless set separately.

SS-DNS-DMARC-002.impact: p=none gathers reports without blocking anything. It is the right first step, but it does not stop anyone from sending mail as your domain.

fixes.label: Tighten the policy once reports look clean

verify: Read the aggregate reports and confirm only your own senders appear.
Change p=none to p=quarantine, then p=reject.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-DMARC-002.limitations: This is a good-practice item and does not reduce the score.

SS-DNS-CAA-001.impact: Any public certificate authority can issue a certificate for the domain if it is tricked or compromised. A CAA record narrows that to the authorities you use.
SS-DNS-CAA-001.detectionNote: The domain has no CAA record.
verify: Run: dig +short CAA <your-domain> and confirm the record is returned.
Renew or issue a certificate to confirm it still works.
Run a new scan.
SS-DNS-CAA-001.limitations: This is a good-practice item and does not reduce the score. Some hosts issue certificates from several authorities, so check before adding the record.

SS-DNS-DNSSEC-001.impact: Without DNSSEC, a resolver cannot tell a forged DNS answer from a real one. This is a hardening step, not a flaw in your site.
SS-DNS-DNSSEC-001.detectionNote: The parent zone publishes no DS record for the domain.

fixes.label: Enable it at your DNS provider, then at the registrar
fixes.code:
1. Turn on DNSSEC in your DNS provider's dashboard.
2. Copy the DS record it shows.
3. Add that DS record at your domain registrar.

verify: Run: dig +short DS <your-domain> and confirm a record is returned.
